newsitem.title: BELARUS: Druzhba oil flows to Germany, Poland, leak stopped.
newsitem.headline: Druzhba oil flows to Germany, Poland, leak stopped.

text.p: Russian oil is flowing to Western Europe through two branches of the Belarus Druzhba pipeline while a third branch which sprung a leak is being repaired, a duty officer at Belarus's state oil company said on Thursday.
The Belnefteprodukt officer said oil was no longer leaking from from the line, which burst on Tuesday evening, spilling hundreds of tonnes of oil in eastern Belarus.
"We've collected almost 200 tonnes -- that's about half of all the spilled oil," the official said by telephone.
"The clean-up is intensive, and estimates of final damage will be completed soon."
The Belarus Druzhba pipeline carries Russian oil to Poland, Germany and the Baltic states and has an annual transit capacity of 35 million tonnes.
A gap in the pipe caused a leak on Tuesday evening near the city of Gomel, 300 kms from the capital of Minsk.
There is a second Druzhba pipeline which carries Russian oil through Ukraine to Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and states of the former Yugoslavia. It was not involved in the accident.
